subject: Hosted API - sudden tokens/sec regression & p99 spikes (Arcadia Commerce)
messages:
From: Ben Wallace <ben.w@arcadia-commerce.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: SaaSInfraOps <ops@arcadia-commerce.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: production regressions this morning - urgent

Hi Naomi,

We started seeing a noticeable slowdown in our checkout recommendation calls this morning around 08:40 PDT. Our dashboards show p95 and p99 latency spikes (p99 up ~3-4x baseline) and overall tokens-per-second from the Redwood endpoint dropped by ~60% for requests to model:rdw-13b-v2. This started immediately after the maintenance window you had scheduled last night.

This is causing queued requests on our side and checkout timeouts for high-concurrency shoppers. Can you confirm whether a config or kernel change was rolled to hosted for rdw-13b-v2? We need a mitigation path and an ETA — this is impacting our Black Friday readiness testing next week.

Attached is a quick screenshot of our latency dashboard and a sample token-rate log. Please escalate to engineering and let me know next steps; we may need traffic reroute or rollback.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Wallace
Head of Platform
Arcadia Commerce

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood-inference.com>

Subject: Fwd: production regressions this morning - urgent

Team — Ben from Arcadia flagged a significant p95/p99 regression + tokens/sec sag against rdw-13b-v2 starting ~08:40 PDT. He called out that it began right after our maintenance window.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: can you confirm whether the kernel/quantization tweak for rdw-13b-v2 was pushed to hosted last night and list the exact commits/configs?
- Markus: please advise whether we have an automatic fallback (model variant or earlier kernel) we can route Arcadia to while we triage.
- Laura: FYI — Arcadia is a high-touch customer preparing for heavy load next week; they want ETA for rollback or mitigation.

I am copying Ben back and will coordinate, but please reply with status ASAP (10–15 min cadence).

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman

naomi.feldman@redwood-inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood-inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: production regressions this morning - urgent

Naomi/Markus — quick update from infra: we did a targeted kernel selector experiment last night that adjusted the attention kernel for rdw-13b-v2 on a subset (~20%) of hosted serving pools to a new fused kernel optimized for low-memory servers. That rollout started at 02:35 PDT and finished by 04:05 PDT. No global config changes beyond that rollout.

Preliminary findings:
- The new kernel improved median latency on microbenchmarks but had unexpectedly poor continuous-batching behavior for long-sequence requests; token/s throughput drops observed in logs where sequence lengths exceeded 800 tokens.
- We see the same tokens/sec sag in the logs Arcadia attached across their calls (matching kernel rollout timestamp).
- Attached: kernel-swap-diff.patch (small config diff) and a short extract of the host logs showing token rate decline.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Roll back kernel selector for rdw-13b-v2 to the previous kernel on affected pools (low-risk, 20–30 min rollback + validation).
2) Route Arcadia traffic to an older model build (rdw-13b-v1-compatible variant) where the previous kernel is active (fast to switch at the router level but may slightly change output distribution).
3) Apply a temporary request-length cap at the load balancer to avoid the long-sequence case (stopgap, will affect some Arcadia use-cases).

I recommend option 2 as fastest for Arcadia specifically, with a parallel rollback (option 1) for global stability. I'm standing by to run rollback if we greenlight.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com

From: Ben Wallace <ben.w@arcadia-commerce.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: SaaSInfraOps <ops@arcadia-commerce.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production regressions this morning - urgent

Thanks Naomi and Rishi — we appreciate the quick triage. Routing to an older model variant (option 2) is acceptable as a short-term mitigation; we need minimal output drift. Please confirm how quickly you can flip routing, and whether we should expect cold-start or throttling during the switch.

Also, can you confirm whether this is eligible for a SLA credit? We logged additional timeouts on our end. I've attached our SLA request doc.

Ben

Attachments: arcadia_request_SLA.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ben Wallace <ben.w@arcadia-commerce.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Oct 2026 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: production regressions this morning - urgent

Ben — we can flip Arcadia to the v1-compatible variant within ~12 minutes; routing change is a config flip with graceful draining, no heavy cold-start expected because variant is warmed in the same pool. We'll monitor token/sec and p99 in real time and keep you updated.

On SLA credit: Laura, can you start the SLA eligibility review and confirm the next steps to process Arcadia's request?

Rishi will push the routing change if we get the go-ahead.

Naomi

Ben — thanks for the patience. Quick update on the SLA/operational side: we've agreed to route Arcadia to the rdw-13b-v1-compatible variant (completed at 10:40 PDT on 2026-10-17). Post-switch telemetry shows tokens/sec and p99 moved back to baseline within ~8 minutes. We've opened JIRA INF-3921 to track the kernel selector revert and a postmortem.

SLA: we've accepted Arcadia's request for a formal review. Our billing & legal teams will reach out by EOD Monday to finalize details; I'll own shepherding that. For damage control, we will provide an operational credit for the impacted window while we complete the root cause postmortem.

Markus/Rishi — please include a timeline for the planned kernel selector revert in INF-3921 and an explicit test plan for long-sequence continuous-batching behavior.

Laura Bennett
